newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Indonesia allocates 700,000 bbls more April LSWR.
newsitem.headline: Indonesia allocates 700,000 bbls more April LSWR.

text.p: Indonesia's state-owned oil company Pertamina has allocated an additional 700,000 barrels of low sulphur waxy residue (LSWR) to its affiliates for April loading, industry sources said on Friday.
The extra allocation is expected to add further downward pressure on prices in an already bearish market as regional demand is at a seasonal low.
Sources were hard pressed to explain the extra cargoes as there no reports of refineries having problems with their crackers.
"The stock built up as some allocations are carried forward and as some people underlift over the past two months," one source said.
As a result, prices have slumped from to below $15.50 per barrel from an early week high of $16.25, traders said.
Pertamina initially allocated 3.6 million barrels for loading in April and the extra barrels will bring the April total to 4.3 million barrels, they said.
The volume is lower than the initial allocation for March at 3.7 million barrels but traders said around 400,000-500,000 barrels scheduled for March lifting had been rolled over for lifting in April.
There was also about one million barrels of straight-run LSWR available from Singapore and Malaysia in April, they said.
Traders said bearish sentiment will prevail for sometime as supplies were much higher than usual with demand extremely poor, especially from Japan, where Pertamina's LSWR is predominantly sold.
"I think demand from Japan will pick up in May when the summer season starts," said one trader, expecting prices to slide further in the meantime and test the $15 per barrel support soon.
A more pessimistic view was offered by one LSWR trader in Tokyo who said he did not expect demand from Japan to pick up until June.
"I think Japanese companies will only start enquiries in June for the summer season between July and September," the Japanese trader said.
Traders said the results from the upcoming Korean Electric Power Corp's (KEPCO) tender to buy 1.2 million barrels of LSWR would be a market indication.
KEPCO is seeking to buy two 600,000-barrel cargoes for June delivery. The tender closes April 15 and is valid for one day.
The company last purchased 500,000 barrels of May LSWR from Dutch trader Vitol at $18.55 per barrel for delivery between May 11-15 to the ports of Ulsan or Pusan on a cost-and-freight basis.
